clue.text: Bird circling lake, quail

indicators.note: the bird's name goes around the lake's letter, so circling signals a container

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird of prey wheels over a lake, eyeing a quail below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' looks like a second bird but is the verb, to shrink back in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to recoil in fear, a synonym of shrinking back.

clue.text: Fruit given to wee little person?

parts.note: a fig is a soft sweet fruit
wee is informal for urine

explanation.surface: Someone hands a piece of fruit to a tiny person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' poses as Scots for small, beside 'little'; it is the noun for urine.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurine is a small statuette of a human, a miniature body; the question mark flags the playful description.

clue.text: Single impression, state, a dead ringer

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I
a dent is an impression pressed into a surface
a means one, again the Roman numeral I
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A lone print of a stamp is a perfect likeness of the original.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are not in clue order: 'a' gives the second I, placed before CAL, the abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: Something called a dead ringer for another looks exactly the same, alike in every detail.

clue.text: Container, for example

explanation.definitionFit: A case is a box or holder, and a case is also an instance, like an example cited.

clue.text: Doctor predicts final state of play, perhaps?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician forecasts how a match will end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of 'predicts'; it is a verb telling you to rearrange that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A play reaches its final written form once the dialogue is fixed on paper, so it is the finished state of a drama.

clue.text: Winter vehicle a jerk overturned, these built for strength

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole string is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a sled is a snow vehicle
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A sledge tipped over by a sudden jolt, while sturdy fortresses stand nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'overturned', flips the whole run SLED+A+TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Citadels are fortresses, strongholds raised for defence.

clue.text: Scrambling three ones entails having to assign values, primarily

indicators.note: scrambling mixes up the letters of the pieces that follow

parts.note: three ones are three Roman numeral I's

explanation.surface: Jumbling a few digits brings the need to set numbers first, in a computing manual.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is III plus ENTAILS, ten letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: In programming, to give variables their starting values before use is the first step of setting up.

clue.text: Expressing disapproval, no good missing term in music

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so missing term means the final letter goes
no placed before good means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: tutting is clicking the tongue in disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone tuts disapprovingly at a missing word in a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from TUTTING, giving TUTTIN, and 'missing term' removes its end letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a score direction meaning all players together, used only in musical notation.

clue.text: Day ending in torpor bound to drag

indicators.note: ending in picks out the final letter of the following word

parts.note: a bound is a boundary or edge

explanation.surface: A day of lethargy ends with someone tied up and pulled along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like tied up; it is a noun meaning limit, EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge is to drag a net or scoop along a riverbed.

clue.text: Hate to remove leader from platform

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for platform is dropped

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: Someone loathes being forced to oust a speaker from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust felt toward someone.

clue.text: Visitor announced, as predicted

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A caller arrives just as everyone had foreseen.
explanation.definitionFit: To have guessed is to have forecast without proof.

clue.text: Fresh start given to holder of pea plant

indicators.note: the word gets a new first letter in place of its old one

parts.note: a referee's whistle holds a small ball called a pea

explanation.surface: Sowing anew around a pea plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holder of pea' is a whistle, which has a pea inside; 'Fresh start given to' swaps its W for T, a letter the clue leaves to the crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: A thistle is a prickly flowering weed, Scotland's emblem.

clue.text: Consider pace

explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to judge or regard, and rate is also speed or tempo.

clue.text: Motor sport where evidently nervous about bid to make a move

indicators.note: about means around, so the nervous word surrounds the rest

parts.note: quaking means trembling with nerves

indicators.note: the letters of bid are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A jittery racer nervously decides to bid and go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a move' is the anagram signal on 'bid'; 'where evidently' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding four-wheeled off-road motorcycles is a motorised leisure pursuit.

clue.text: Babes naked in an orgy, saucy thing

indicators.note: an orgy is a wild jumble, so the letters are thrown together anew

explanation.surface: Unclothed women at a wild party, a risque scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' looks like risque but means in tomato sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricots in tomato sauce, a tinned staple, are a food coated in sauce.

clue.text: Sweet thing finds sticky thing past the Centre of Birmingham

indicators.note: past means after, so the sticky thing comes after the centre

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
tar is a sticky black substance

explanation.surface: A sweet treat is found stuck to a pavement beyond the middle of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of Birmingham' suggests the middle letters; it is the NEC, Birmingham's National Exhibition Centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the sugary fluid flowers produce, also any delicious drink.

clue.text: Howl in grief with which backing singer consumed

indicators.note: backing means turned back, so the singer's name runs right to left

parts.note: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A backing vocalist who ate too much wails mournfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing singer' reads as a support vocalist, but 'backing' reverses LULU to ULUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to wail with a high trilling cry of lament.

clue.text: System on course has to charm, with no man above the Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue above means placed before the next piece
with no means the man's letters are taken out of the charm

parts.note: a talisman is a lucky charm
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A racecourse betting operation charms punters, minus a man, beneath royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: A totaliser, or tote, is the betting machine at a racecourse. 'with no' signals the deletion and 'above' places the shortened charm first in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser is the pool-betting machine at a racetrack that shares out stakes among winners.

clue.text: Clergyman has his subject to sell, embracing the same

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the clergyman's subject

indicators.note: embracing means the selling word wraps around the repeated letters

parts.note: vend means to sell
the same means those two letters again

explanation.surface: A priest trades in his specialist topic while embracing it fully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' means the clergyman's subject repeated, and 'embracing' puts that repeat inside the word for sell, between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverend is a minister, a title for priests.

clue.text: Type of word with old number, forbidden

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on an old numeral turns out to be off-limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Verboten is German for prohibited, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Is one out on one's ear?

definitions.text: Is one out on one's ear?

parts.words: Is one out on one's ear?
parts.note: out on one's ear usually means thrown out, but here it means unconscious while lying on the side of the head

explanation.definitionFit: Someone dead to the world in bed, resting their head on the pillow, is a slumberer.

clue.text: Fly lays first of eggs on head of tourist

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the tourist

parts.note: sets means puts down or lays

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of eggs

explanation.surface: A fly lays its first eggs on a tourist's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of tourist' gives T, then SETS, then E from 'first of eggs'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Trip up going round to journalist

indicators.note: going round means the reversed trip encloses the next word
up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ride is a trip

explanation.surface: A journalist trips up while out and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the trip in this down clue, giving EDIR, and 'going round' wraps it around 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a newspaper's chief, a senior figure on the paper.

clue.text: Opt for stout

explanation.definitionFit: To plump for is to choose, and plump means chubby, of rounded build.

clue.text: Insect given nudge with betel nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A bug is nudged towards some betel nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the nuts of the betel palm but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dung beetle is a scarab that rolls balls of animal droppings.

clue.text: Neither pa is a girl

parts.note: the phrase neither pa calls for its completion, starting with nor
the other parent in the stock phrase is ma

explanation.surface: Neither father counts as a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neither pa' invites the rest of the phrase, nor ma.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female forename, as in Bellini's opera heroine.

clue.text: Strike union

explanation.definitionFit: To club is to hit with a stick, and a club is a society or association.

clue.text: Pass over a drink

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass over' reads as skip; here COL sits over A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with kola nut.

clue.text: Order caterer for a number of houses

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Booking a caterer for several homes on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined dwellings, common in British streets.

clue.text: Doctor beginning lowering of heavenly body

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
an onset is a beginning

explanation.surface: A medic starts to watch a planet sinking out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonset is when the lunar disc disappears below the horizon.

clue.text: Taking chances in bar, Yankee finding ecstasy

indicators.note: in means the chances sit inside the bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar
haps are chance events
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American gambles in a pub and finds bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; it is ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsody is a state of rapture or delighted enthusiasm.

clue.text: Rumoured aristocrat unable to produce heirs?

indicators.note: rumoured means said by word of mouth, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A gossiped-about noble cannot father an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren means infertile, incapable of bearing children.
